name: Cloud Gate ("The Bean")

practical_tip: Go early morning to beat crowds for a clean shot — the #1 tip repeated across creator content. The 2025 'Man in the Bean' hoax is now dated meme history, not a current draw, so don't lead with it as if it's still trending.

why_tiktok: Still the most photographed landmark in the sweep; was also the site of the 2025 'Man in the Bean' viral hoax

name: Adler Planetarium (north lawn / Solar Terrace)
address: 1300 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
rating_note: No single aggregate rating applies (it's open grounds, not a listed business); Adler Planetarium itself carries strong general praise across guides. Grounds access confirmed free and open per adlerplanetarium.org.
closed_days: Grounds never close; museum interior hours vary (11am-4pm typical, Wed 4pm-10pm, Fri-Mon 9am opening) per adlerplanetarium.org/visit/your-visit/hours
price_band: Free (grounds); museum admission separate if going inside
signature: Stand on the grass point behind/north of the Adler building for a wide-open skyline + Lake Michigan shot with no obstructions; go right at sunset so the skyline lights up as the sky darkens
why_tiktok: It's the single most-repeated 'best skyline view in Chicago' claim on travel TikTok — flat, unobstructed foreground with the whole downtown skyline across the water, plus free after-hours access to the grounds even when the museum is closed
practical_tip: Go 30-45 min before sunset, stay past dusk for the skyline lighting up; grounds free even when museum closed; Wednesday evening opening (4-10pm) is a bonus for after-dark shots
verdict_reason: Confirmed real, free, open location; multiple independent guides corroborate the exact vantage point and best-time advice.

name: Ping Tom Memorial Park

rating_note: Google rating not individually confirmed in this search pass; TripAdvisor listing exists with generally positive user reviews describing skyline views as a highlight.

why_tiktok: Framed repeatedly on TikTok as an 'underrated'/hidden-gem skyline spot outside the typical downtown tourist loop, with Chinese-inspired architecture giving a distinctive foreground; also went viral as the meeting point for the 'Hot Girl Walk' trend
practical_tip: Best light is summer sunset over the river; take the water taxi from downtown in warm months instead of driving/parking
verdict_reason: Real, free, open park; skyline-view claim corroborated independently by TripAdvisor reviews, not just TikTok.

name: Indiana Dunes National Park (beach mirage view of Chicago skyline)
address: Indiana Dunes Visitor Center, 1215 N State Rd 49, Porter, IN 46304
rating_note: Not individually rated as a viewpoint; the park itself is well-reviewed generally, but this is a weather-dependent phenomenon, not a fixed attraction.
closed_days: Park open daily; the mirage effect itself is NOT guaranteed on any visit
price_band: $25/vehicle (1-7 day pass) or $15/person walk-in — confirmed via nps.gov / indianadunes.com fee pages
signature: On a clear, calm day with the right temperature-inversion conditions, the Chicago skyline appears to float above the horizon across the lake — a 'superior mirage' effect that makes the skyline visible from far beyond normal sightline distance
why_tiktok: Viral optical-illusion content: creators post videos captioned along the lines of 'you can see Chicago from 33/50 miles away' showing the skyline floating on the water horizon, explained as a superior mirage phenomenon
practical_tip: The entrance fee is real ($25/vehicle, confirmed 2026) and the mirage is NOT reliable — it requires a specific temperature inversion that happens only a handful of days a year. Don't sell this as a guaranteed sight; frame as a rare bonus, not a planned itinerary stop.
verdict_reason: Real park with a real, well-documented mirage phenomenon, but it is rare/weather-dependent and now carries a confirmed $25/vehicle fee — both meaningfully undercut it as a reliable travel-guide recommendation.

The 'TikTok evidence' in the original brief was actually a travel-guide article, not a TikTok post — treat the viral claim as unconfirmed.
verdict_reason: The location and view are real, but the TikTok-virality claim has no direct source (guide-article only) and the bridge has a real history of unpredictable closures.

name: Old Joliet Prison (abandoned/haunted)
name_zh: 网红监狱 / 越狱拍摄地
address: 1125 Collins St, Joliet, IL 60432
rating_note: Not independently found on Yelp/Google in this pass; site's own visitor info confirms operating status
closed_days: Open daily 10am-4pm for general/self-guided access; guided walking tours are seasonal, April-October only
reservation: Self-guided access walk-in; guided tours (incl. movie/Prison Break-themed tours) require advance booking
price_band: Free (self-guided exterior/grounds); guided tours ticketed separately
verdict_reason: Real and open, and the Prison Break filming-location claim checks out, but access is materially more limited than the TikTok framing implies: guided tours only run April-October, the site is under active construction/preservation with buildings rotating in and out of accessibility, tours are outdoors rain-or-shine, and it is not ADA-approved (only ~70% accessible). A traveler expecting a full indoor cellblock walk-through in winter will be disappointed.
signature: Walk the abandoned cellblocks used as the filming location for the TV show Prison Break.
why_tiktok: Framed in Chinese travel content as a 小众玩法 (off-the-beaten-path activity) distinct from the standard skyline/food circuit.
practical_tip: Requires a car and ~1.5hr round trip from downtown. Guided tours (including the Prison Break-themed ones) run April-October only — outside that window you're limited to self-guided grounds access, and even then some buildings may be roped off for preservation work.
